question: The public-sector organisation Aena has announced that Valencia-Manises and Alicante-Elche airports are to be extended in order to meet growing traffic demand. Extending them will affect both noise pollution levels, in breach of Directive 2002/49/EC and Regulation (EU) No 598/2014, and environmental pollution, as it is contrary to the European Green Deal and to a commitment to more sustainable and cleaner transport. 1.
How will the Commission ensure that Directive 2002/49/EC and Regulation (EU) No 598/2014 are complied with?
Having regard to the issue at stake, what guarantees does the public have that the European Green Deal will be complied with?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2024) Under the European Green Deal1, the Commission put forward a Zero Pollution Action Plan2, including a target of reducing by 30% by 2030 the number of people chronically disturbed by transport noise in respect to 2017. The Commission monitors progress through the Zero Pollution Monitoring and Outlook report3.

The Environmental Noise Directive (END)4 requires Member States to make strategic noise maps and action plans every five years. Strategic noise maps are a basis for measures to address noise pollution and serve to monitor progress towards the noise target. The most recent ones, due by 30 June 2022, were not reported by the Spanish authorities despite the Commission having reminded Spain.

According to Article 8(5) of the END, when a major development occurs affecting the existing noise situation, action plans shall be reviewed and, if necessary, revised. Nevertheless, actions to address priorities identified remain under the discretion of the competent authority. The Commission started infringement proceedings against Spain5, also addressing the gaps for the two airports.

The Commission has issued a reasoned opinion6 and is in the process of assessing the reply of the Spanish authorities. Regulation (EU) 598/20147 sets out rules and procedures with regard to the introduction of noise-related operating restrictions at Union airports. The Commission has not received any notification of noise-related operating restrictions at the airports concerned.
